music_selection_rules.rule: Match scene type to mood examples
music_selection_rules.explanation: Study the scene type classifications above. When you encounter a similar scene (confrontation, revelation, party, etc.), reference which music files were used in the examples.
Dialogue-heavy scenes need lower intensity (40-60). Action scenes can use higher intensity (70-85). Never let music overwhelm dialogue.
Music should start 2-5 seconds BEFORE emotional peak or action begins. Don't wait until the moment - build anticipation.
Never use uplifting music in tragic scenes, playful music in dangerous scenes, or scary music in romantic scenes. Match the emotional reality.

ambience_rules.rule: ONLY match scene header location, NOT mood or dialogue
ambience_rules.correct_example: INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY → cafe ambience
ambience_rules.incorrect_example: Character mentions ocean in dialogue → ocean ambience (WRONG - match header only)

ambience_rules.rule: INT = indoor ambience, EXT = outdoor ambience
ambience_rules.explanation: Never select based on emotions, memories, or what character is talking about. Only match the ACTUAL PHYSICAL LOCATION in the scene header.

ambience_rules.rule: Generic interiors often need NO ambience
ambience_rules.explanation: Living rooms, bedrooms, kitchens do not need ambience unless specific keywords align with database (office phones, hospital PA, etc.)
Description might contradict obvious choice. If description says 'bodies hit floor with debris', ignore 'office' in header and use no ambience.

ambience_rules.rule: Combine files when necessary at 50% volume each
ambience_rules.explanation: Sometimes two ambience files needed for accuracy. Split volume between both files.

ambience_rules.rule: Loop ambience for entire scene duration
ambience_rules.explanation: If ambience file shorter than scene, loop it until scene ends.

voice_selection_rules.rule: AGE DETERMINES LABEL - This is the most critical rule
age_mappings: Under 10 years old = 'Male Under 10' or 'Female Under 10'
critical_mistakes: NEVER use 'Male 20s to 30s' for 17-19 year olds - they are still teens
NEVER use 'Male Teen' for someone in their 20s
NEVER use 'Older Male' for someone in their 30s

style_mappings: African American character = African American style voice
Hispanic/Latina character = American style (no specific option)
Asian character = American style (no specific option)
critical_mistakes: NEVER use American style for African American character
NEVER ignore explicit ethnicity descriptors in script

tone_guidelines: Authority figures = Deep or Stern or Wise
Young energetic = Bubbly or Playful or Energetic

voice_selection_rules.explanation: Male character = Male voice. Female character = Female voice. Never cross genders.
Voiceover narration (V.O.) uses Narrator label, not character labels. Even if character is narrating their own story, use Narrator voice for V.O. sections.

common_error_patterns.error: Using 'Male 20s to 30s' for 17-18 year old characters
common_error_patterns.why_its_wrong: Teen voices sound distinctly different from adult voices. Age 17-18 are still developmental teenage years.
common_error_patterns.correct_approach: Always use 'Male Teen' for ages 11-19, even if they're 18-19

common_error_patterns.why_its_wrong: Script specifically describes character ethnicity for authenticity
common_error_patterns.correct_approach: Match African American characters to African American style voices

common_error_patterns.error: Using soft/breathy tones for confident characters
common_error_patterns.correct_approach: Football captain = deep voice, not breathy. Cheerleader = bubbly, not calm.

common_error_patterns.error: Using character voice for their V.O. narration
common_error_patterns.correct_approach: Use Narrator label for all V.O. sections, even if character is narrating
